snippet: A tourniquet is a device that applies pressure to a limb or extremity in order to limit, but not stop, the flow of blood. It may be used in emergencies, in surgery, or in post-operative rehabilitation.
title: Tourniquet

snippet: Apply the tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound, never over a joint. Tighten until bleeding stops. Note the time of application on the tourniquet and on the casualty card.
title: Tourniquet (hemorrhage control)

snippet: Water purification is the process of removing undesirable chemicals, biological contaminants, suspended solids, and gases from water. Methods include boiling, filtration, chemical disinfection and distillation.
title: Water purification

snippet: Hypothermia is a medical emergency that occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it, causing a dangerously low body temperature. Normal body temperature is around 37 C (98.6 F).
title: Hypothermia

snippet: Amateur radio is a popular hobby and service that brings people, electronics and communication together. People use ham radio to talk across town, around the world, or even into space, all without the Internet or cell phones.
title: Amateur radio

snippet: Home canning is the process of preserving food in sealed jars. Low-acid foods must be processed in a pressure canner; high-acid foods may be processed in a boiling-water canner.
title: Home canning

snippet: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is an emergency procedure consisting of chest compressions often combined with artificial ventilation, performed to manually preserve brain function until further measures can restore spontaneous blood circulation and breathing.
title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation

snippet: A topographic map is a type of map characterized by large-scale detail and quantitative representation of relief features, usually using contour lines, but historically using a variety of methods.
title: Topographic map
